# CHAT.md — Chat Interface Architecture & Implementation Plan > **Context**: This document captures my thorough review of the Aevryn codebase and outlines what needs to be built to create a fully agentic chat interface using Vercel AI SDK, real tools, and the durable Inngest execution engine. --- ## Part 1: Codebase Observations ### 1.1 Architecture Overview (Single-User Pivot) The system has been re-architected from a multi-user tRPC backend to a **single-user agentic chat platform**: ``` Browser (Next.js + Zustand) → POST /api/chat (Vercel AI SDK streamText) → Live tools (askQuestion, showPlan, editPlan, memory, httpRequest) → Durable delegate: inngest.send("thread/run") → Inngest thread-runner fn → Supabase Realtime → run_activities stream into chat ``` **Key Architectural Decisions:** - **Single-user only**: No workspace_members, invites, thread_shares. Each user owns exactly one "Personal" workspace. - **Two execution paths**: Live (fast tools via streamText) + Durable (long-running via Inngest) - **One assistant message**: Tool results append to the SAME message bubble (no new bubbles for sub-steps) - **New chat message triggers**: Only on error, warning, workflow stop, or user clicking Run again ### 1.2 Database Schema (packages/db) **16 Tables, Single-User Design:** | Table | Purpose | Key Fields | Phase | | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | | `workspaces` | User's own workspace (1 per user, "Personal") | id, name, created_by, is_default | — | | `workspace_settings` | Workspace-level config (NEW) | id, workspace_id, groq_key, model_name, auto_approve_default, theme | Phase 1 | | `groups` | Workflow groups (containers for threads) | id, workspace_id, user_id, name, kind | — | | `threads` | Chat threads (a thread = a workflow after binding) | id, workspace_id, group_id, user_id, title, bound_workflow_id, deleted_at | — | | `thread_settings` | Thread-level config overrides (NEW) | id, thread_id, system_prompt, token_slider_default | Phase 1 | | `workflows` | Workflow definitions with plans | id, thread_id, workspace_id, user_id, title, status, auto_approve | — | | `plans` | Plan attached to a workflow | id, workflow_id, title, objective, summary, status | — | | `plan_steps` | Individual steps in a plan | id, plan_id, position, title, description, status | — | | `chat_messages` | Conversation history | id, thread_id, user_id, role, content (JSONB), run_id, status, queue_order | — | | `runs` | Execution runs (durable or live) | id, thread_id, workflow_id, user_id, trigger, status, cost_usd, token_count | — | | `run_activities` | Live activity stream (ThinkingSteps) | id, run_id, type, status, step_label, title, detail | — | | `approval_requests` | Tool approval gates | id, run_id, user_id, tool_name, input, status | — | | `schedules` | Cron/interval scheduled runs | id, workspace_id, thread_id, user_id, cron, interval_seconds, next_run_at | — | | `webhook_hooks` | External webhook waitpoints | id, run_id, workspace_id, thread_id, url, instruction, expires_at | DROPPED (MVP) | | `notifications` | User notifications | id, user_id, workspace_id, thread_id, type, title, body, read_at | — | | `workspace_api_keys` | API key vault (plaintext in MVP) | id, workspace_id, provider, key, model_name | Phase 5 (encrypt→plaintext) | | `user_profiles` | User profile + onboarding | id, user_id, name, email, pfp, onboarded, pre_answers, plan | — | > **Note on settings tables**: `workspace_settings` and `thread_settings` don't exist yet — they're being added in Phase 1 to support the Settings dialog (Workspace + Global split) and Thread Settings dialog. Before each phase, the Drizzle schema files are updated and `drizzle-kit generate` is run to produce the SQL migration. The user applies migrations manually. **Critical Enums (combined RUN_STATUSES = WORKFLOW_STATUSES):** ```typescript RUN_STATUSES = [ "running", "sleeping", "awaiting_approval", "failed", "completed", "idle", "planning", "stopped", ]; MESSAGE_STATUSES = [ "draft", "queued", "streaming", "completed", "failed", "interrupted", ]; ACTIVITY_TYPES = ["tool", "thinking", "task", "subtask", "system"]; ACTIVITY_STATUSES = ["pending", "active", "complete", "failed"]; RUN_TRIGGERS = ["message", "schedule", "resume", "approval", "rerun"]; API_PROVIDERS = [ "groq", "anakin", "mem0", "image", "speech", "transcription", "video", ]; ``` ### 1.3 Agent Package (packages/agent) **Core Concepts:** 1. **Capability Registry Pattern**: Tools are registered as `Capability` objects with: - `name`, `description`, `inputSchema` (Zod), `outputSchema?`, `requiresApproval?` - `execute(input)` → `CapabilityResult` (success/failure with structured data) 2. **Two Execution Modes**: - **Live (`runAgent`)**: Uses `generateText` from Vercel AI SDK with tool calls, maxSteps cap, toolApproval gate - **Durable (`thread-runner`)**: Inngest function, same tools minus re-delegation, persists every step to DB 3. **Chat Tools (9 total)** — all defined in `packages/agent/src/chat/tools.ts`: | Tool | Type | Purpose | |------|------|---------| | `listCapabilities` | Live | List available tools (meta) | | `askQuestion` | Live | Ask user MCQ question, pause for reply | | `showPlan` | Live | Show bound workflow's plan | | `editPlan` | Live | Add/update/remove plan steps | | `bindWorkflow` | Live | Create workflow+plan from objective, bind to thread | | `storeMemory` | Live → mem0 | Store durable fact/preference | | `searchMemory` | Live → mem0 | Recall stored memories | | `httpRequest` | Live | Raw HTTP with caps (SSRf safe) | | `delegateAgenticWork` | Durable → Inngest | Hand off to thread/run | 4. **Prompt Library** (`packages/agent/src/prompts.ts`): - `SYSTEM_PERSONA` — Immutable persona - `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` — Tool usage rules (NO auto-plan, prefer tools over speculation) - `PLANNING_SYSTEM` — Planning mode instructions - `DURABLE_RUNNER_SYSTEM` + `RUN_DECISION_INSTRUCTIONS` — Durable agent prompts - `buildSystem()` — Composes prompts with workflow context, auto-approve state, memory summary 5. **Anakin Adapters** (10 total): search, scrape, crawl, map, research, wire, browser-session (CRUD) ### 1.4 Inngest Functions (packages/inngest) **Event-Driven, Single Event Model:** ```typescript // ONE event drives everything threadRunEvent = "thread/run" → data: { runId, threadId, prompt, modelContextCapChars?, recoveryContext?, approvedToolNames? } ``` **FunctionsServed (apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts):** 1. **`thread-run`** — The main durable agent: - Resolves run state (idempotent gate: skip if terminal/sleeping/awaiting_approval) - Checks wall-clock + cost + tool-call budgets BEFORE each step - Runs `runAgent` with full toolset + execution capabilities - Persists activities to `run_activities` in real-time - Handles `emitDecision` tool: sleep/notify/stop/wait/complete - Creates approval requests for pending tools - Stores episodic + procedural memory on completion - Triggers queue delivery on completion - Bounded recovery: classifies failure, retries up to RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS 2. **`schedule-tick`** — Cron/interval scheduler: - Fires due schedules → creates run → sends thread/run event - Wakes sleeping runs whose sleepUntil has passed 3. **`queue-deliver`** — Sequential queue drain: - Pops oldest queued message → starts fresh "message" run → sends thread/run - Re-triggers on run finish → next queued message 4. **`notification-notifier`** — Webhook delivery: - Delivers webhook notifications with idempotency marker ### 1.5 Web App UI (apps/web) **Current State:** - **Login screen** (`apps/web/src/app/page.tsx`): Google OAuth via Supabase - **Auth callback** (`apps/web/src/app/auth/callback/route.ts`): Exchanges code, syncs profile, redirects to `/workspace` - **Onboarding** (`apps/web/src/app/onboarding/page.tsx`): QuestionFlow from `questions.json` - **Workspace layout** (`apps/web/src/app/workspace/[workspaceId]/layout.tsx`): SidebarProvider + AppSidebar + Header + children - **Thread page** (`apps/web/src/app/workspace/[workspaceId]/[threadId]/page.tsx`): Currently just ChatComposer placeholder - **Workspace page** (`apps/web/src/app/workspace/[workspaceId]/page.tsx`): Placeholder with image - **Old workspace demo** (`apps/web/src/app/old-workspace/page.tsx`): Full mock chat UI — the reference for the real interface **Key UI Components (EXISTING - need wiring only):** - `AppSidebar` — Real data from Supabase, workspace switcher, search, notifications bell, New button, groups with threads, settings dropdown, theme toggle, user footer - `Header` — Thread dropdown (searchable), in-place rename input - `WorkflowDialog` — Tabbed dialog (General/Plan/Instructions/Memories), mock data currently; **Instructions tab → rename to "Agent"** - `SettingsDialog` — Tabbed dialog (General/Notifications/Appearance/Security); **split into Workspace + Global** - `WorkflowDelConfirmationDialog` — Delete confirmation with item list - `NewThreadDialog`, `NewGroupDialog`, `EntityActionDialog`, `ConfirmDeleteDialog` **Reference UI (old-workspace/page.tsx — the model for the real chat interface):** The old-workspace page is a complete mock of the chat UI. It shows exactly how everything fits together: ``` SidebarProvider AppSidebar SidebarInset WorkflowDialog (open/close state) div.flex.column (full height) header (h-12) SearchableDropdown ← thread selector InputGroup + InputField ← thread title (rename on focus) Button Run ← visible after workflow bound+approved Button Settings ← opens WorkflowDialog section (flex-1, overflow-y-auto) ← conversation area div.max-w-3xl.flex.column div.flex-1.p-4 div.flex.flex-column.gap-2 ← message list ChatMessage from=user ← user bubble ChatMessage from=assistant children = div.gap-5 ← assistant content block p.text ← plain text paragraph QuestionFlow ← askUserQuestions (clarifying Qs) AccordionGroup ← plan steps (collapsible) AccordionItem × N QuestionFlow ← workflowApproval (4 buttons) div.gap-1 ← tool step calls ResearchAgent WebScrapeAgent CompilingAgent FinalAnswerStep Table ← LLM-rendered markdown tables SystemMessage mb-[40px] ← notices (questions submitted, cron scheduled, errors, warnings) footer.p-3 div.max-w-3xl ChatComposer ← input + slider + send ``` **Key patterns from old-workspace:** 1. **Assistant message = one bubble, rich children**: A single `ChatMessage from=assistant` wraps a `div.gap-5` containing mixed content — plain `

` text, `QuestionFlow`, `AccordionGroup` (plan), another `QuestionFlow` (approval), tool step components, and `Table`. This is the ONE assistant message contract. 2. **`mb-[40px]` on SystemMessage**: Every SystemMessage has `mb-[40px]` to create spacing before the next message. Consider a dedicated component or CSS class for this. 3. **QuestionFlow appears multiple times in one conversation**: Clarifying questions (before plan) AND approval questions (after plan) are separate `QuestionFlow` instances in different assistant messages. 4. **Tool steps render inside assistant bubble**: `ResearchAgent`, `WebScrapeAgent`, `CompilingAgent`, `FinalAnswerStep` are `ThinkingSteps` components rendered inline inside the assistant's message children. 5. **LLM can render tables**: The assistant message children include a `` component — the LLM output includes markdown that gets rendered as a table. 6. **ThinkingIndicator placeholder**: A `ChatMessage from=assistant` with just `` shows the thinking state while waiting for the final message. 7. **Header has Run + Settings buttons**: Run appears after workflow is bound+approved; Settings always opens WorkflowDialog. 8. **Thread title is an InputField**: In-place rename via InputField in the header. **Components used in old-workspace (all exist in packages/ui):** | Component | Path | Purpose | |-----------|------|---------| | `ChatComposer` | `@aevryn/ui/components/chat-composer` | Input + token slider + send/queue | | `ChatMessage` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/chat-message` | Message bubble (user/assistant) | | `SystemMessage` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/system-message` | System notices (action/error/warning) | | `QuestionFlow` | `@aevryn/ui/components/question-flow` | MCQ question flow wrapper | | `AskUserQuestions` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/ask-user-questions` | Core question renderer | | `ThinkingSteps` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/thinking-steps` | Collapsible step list | | `ThinkingStep` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/thinking-steps` | Single step with icon/label/description | | `ThinkingStepDetails` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/thinking-steps` | Nested collapsible details | | `ThinkingStepSources` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/thinking-steps` | Source badge container | | `ThinkingStepSource` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/thinking-steps` | Individual source badge | | `ThinkingStepImage` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/thinking-steps` | Image with caption | | `ThinkingIndicator` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/thinking-indicator` | Animated thinking placeholder | | `AccordionGroup/Item/Trigger/Content` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/accordion` | Plan steps accordion | | `Table/TableHeader/TableBody/TableRow/TableHead/TableCell` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/table` | LLM-rendered tables | | `WorkflowDialog` | `@aevryn/ui/components/dialog/workflow-dialog` | Workflow settings dialog | | `SearchableDropdown` | `@aevryn/ui/components/header/searchable-dropdown` | Thread selector | | `InputGroup/InputField` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/input-group` | Thread title input | | `Button` | `@aevryn/ui/components/ui/button` | Run/Settings buttons | **Mock tool-step components (apps/web/src/components/workspace/tool-step-calls.tsx):** These are demo wrappers around `ThinkingSteps` showing how tool activity renders. They'll be replaced by real data from `run_activities`. - `ResearchAgent` — ThinkingSteps with search + image + reading steps - `WebScrapeAgent` — ThinkingSteps with scraping + extraction steps - `CompilingAgent` — ThinkingSteps with comparison + ranking steps - `FinalAnswerStep` — ThinkingSteps with single generation step **To Wire/Integrate (components exist, need chat integration):** - `ChatComposer` — Main chat input (text, token slider, send/queue buttons) — NO attachments in MVP; **wire in-place in packages/ui** - `ChatMessage` — Already wired, renders UIMessage parts (text, tool calls) — plain text only in MVP - `SystemMessage` — Already wired, system notices with mb-40 spacing pattern - `AskUserQuestions` / `QuestionFlow` — Already wired, MCQ question UI - `WorkflowApproval` — Use `QuestionFlow` + `AskUserQuestions` with approval schema (Approve/Decline/Bind/Request changes) - `ThinkingSteps` — Already wired, renders run_activities as live steps; replace mock tool-step-calls with real data - `ProfileDialog` — User profile with pre_answers, plan badge, delete account - `NotificationsDialog` — Real notifications list + unread chip **Thread Settings Dialog (NEW — reuse WorkflowDialog pattern):** - Create `thread-settings-dialog.tsx` reusing the same Sidebar-dialog shell as `workflow-dialog.tsx` - Sections: General (thread name), Agent (system prompt, auto_approve), Environment (Groq/Anakin/Mem0 keys per workspace), Export/Import - Same `WorkflowSectionPanel` pattern → `ThreadSectionPanel` with per-section components - Open from sidebar, above Global Settings, named "Thread Settings" **Zustand stores to create (for state management, keeping server components pure):** - `useAuthStore` — User session, profile - `useThreadStore` — Current thread, messages, run status - `useComposerStore` — Input text, token slider value - `useSidebarStore` — Workspaces, groups, threads, notifications count - `useNotificationsStore` — Unread count, notifications list - `useUIStore` — Modal open states, theme ### 1.6 Chat API Route (apps/web/src/app/api/chat/route.ts) **Current Implementation (already substantial):** ```typescript POST /api/chat → requireUser (Supabase auth) → validate chatBodySchema (threadId?, workspaceId?, message, autoApprove?, maxOutputTokens?) NOTE: attachments removed for MVP - plain text only → resolve thread (create if new) → resolve Groq key (workspace vault → env) → check queue: if active run → enqueue message, return {queued: true} NOTE: Queue feature dropped for MVP - messages send immediately always → insert user message + streaming assistant message to DB → auto-title thread on first message → create turn run (status: running) → buildUIMessages from history → createChatTools with services + onDelegateWork callback → streamText({ model: groq.languageModel(modelName), system: buildChatSystemPrompt(), messages, tools, maxOutputTokens }) → persistAssistantMessage in background (tool results + text → DB) → toUIMessageStream → createUIMessageStreamResponse ``` **What's Already Working:** - Auth guard, thread resolution/creation - Groq model resolution from workspace keys (per-workspace, future-proof for multi-workspace) - Tool creation with all 9 chat tools - Durable delegation (inngest.send("thread/run")) - Streaming response via Vercel AI SDK - Activity persistence to run_activities **MVP Simplifications:** - NO attachments (no image/pdf/video upload) - NO queue feature (messages send immediately, no queuing) - NO image/speech/transcription/video model configs (text-only via Groq) ### 1.7 Auth Flow (packages/auth) - **Supabase Auth** with Google OAuth only (MVP) - `createBrowserSupabase()` for client, `createServerSupabase()` for server - Session via `@supabase/ssr` cookies - Profile sync on login (name, email, pfp → user_profiles) - Onboarding trigger if profile missing or not onboarded ### 1.8 Zustand + Realtime Architecture **Planned Store Architecture (Zustand for client state, keeping server components pure):** - `useAuthStore` — User session, profile - `useThreadStore` — Current thread, messages, run status - `useComposerStore` — Input text, token slider value (NO queue, NO attachments in MVP) - `useSidebarStore` — Workspaces, groups, threads, notifications count - `useNotificationsStore` — Unread count, notifications list - `useUIStore` — Modal open states, theme **Realtime Subscriptions:** - `chat_messages` on `thread:{threadId}` — New messages appear live - `run_activities` on `thread:{threadId}` — ThinkingSteps stream in real-time - `approval_requests` on `thread:{threadId}` — Approval dialog triggers - `notifications` on `user:{userId}` — Bell chip updates (cross-thread) --- ## Part 2: What Needs to Be Built (MVP - Simplified) ### 2.1 Core Chat Interface (Must Build) #### A. ChatComposer Component **Location**: `apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx` **MVP Features (NO attachments, NO queue):** 1. **Centered → Bottom transition**: Start centered on empty thread, shift to bottom after first message 2. **Text input only**: Multi-line, send on Enter (Shift+Enter for newline) 3. **Token quality slider**: Maps to `maxOutputTokens` for the chat request (NOT run budget) - Store `quality` in Zustand, NOT in DropdownMenu (pointer-events bug) 4. **Send behavior**: Always send immediately via useChat → /api/chat (NO queue in MVP) #### B. ChatMessage Component **Location**: `apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatMessage.tsx` **MVP Features (plain text only):** - Render UIMessage parts: - `text` → plain text (future: markdown parser for tables etc.) - `tool-*` → tool call visualization (when LLM calls tools) - NO file attachments, NO image/media support in MVP #### C. # Skill: webapp-testing

# Web Application Testing

To test local web applications, write native Python Playwright scripts.

**Helper Scripts Available**:
- `scripts/with_server.py` - Manages server lifecycle (supports multiple servers)

**Always run scripts with `--help` first** to see usage. DO NOT read the source until you try running the script first and find that a customized solution is abslutely necessary. These scripts can be very large and thus pollute your context window. They exist to be called directly as black-box scripts rather than ingested into your context window.

## Decision Tree: Choosing Your Approach

```
User task → Is it static HTML?
    ├─ Yes → Read HTML file directly to identify selectors
    │         ├─ Success → Write Playwright script using selectors
    │         └─ Fails/Incomplete → Treat as dynamic (below)
    │
    └─ No (dynamic webapp) → Is the server already running?
        ├─ No → Run: python scripts/with_server.py --help
        │        Then use the helper + write simplified Playwright script
        │
        └─ Yes → Reconnaissance-then-action:
            1. Navigate and wait for networkidle
            2. Take screenshot or inspect DOM
            3. Identify selectors from rendered state
            4. Execute actions with discovered selectors
```

## Example: Using with_server.py

To start a server, run `--help` first, then use the helper:

**Single server:**
```bash
python scripts/with_server.py --server "npm run dev" --port 5173 -- python your_automation.py
```

**Multiple servers (e.g., backend + frontend):**
```bash
python scripts/with_server.py \
  --server "cd backend && python server.py" --port 3000 \
  --server "cd frontend && npm run dev" --port 5173 \
  -- python your_automation.py
```

To create an automation script, include only Playwright logic (servers are managed automatically):
```python
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True) # Always launch chromium in headless mode
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto('http://localhost:5173') # Server already running and ready
    page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle') # CRITICAL: Wait for JS to execute
    # ... your automation logic
    browser.close()
```

## Reconnaissance-Then-Action Pattern

1. **Inspect rendered DOM**:
   ```python
   page.screenshot(path='/tmp/inspect.png', full_page=True)
   content = page.content()
   page.locator('button').all()
   ```

2. **Identify selectors** from inspection results

3. **Execute actions** using discovered selectors

## Common Pitfall

❌ **Don't** inspect the DOM before waiting for `networkidle` on dynamic apps
✅ **Do** wait for `page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')` before inspection

## Best Practices

- **Use bundled scripts as black boxes** - To accomplish a task, consider whether one of the scripts available in `scripts/` can help. These scripts handle common, complex workflows reliably without cluttering the context window. Use `--help` to see usage, then invoke directly. 
- Use `sync_playwright()` for synchronous scripts
- Always close the browser when done
- Use descriptive selectors: `text=`, `role=`, CSS selectors, or IDs
- Add appropriate waits: `page.wait_for_selector()` or `page.wait_for_timeout()`

## Reference Files

- **examples/** - Examples showing common patterns:
  - `element_discovery.py` - Discovering buttons, links, and inputs on a page
  - `static_html_automation.py` - Using file:// URLs for local HTML
  - `console_logging.py` - Capturing console logs during automation

202:  * - all workspaces created by the user (workspace switcher)
203:  * - the current workspace's groups (name + position, ordered) and their
204:  *   non-deleted threads (group id, bound workflow id, title), ordered by
205:  *   last message time.
206:  * RLS scopes every query to the signed-in user.
207:  *
208:  * After the initial fetch, a workspace-scoped realtime channel keeps the
209:  * groups + threads in sync for INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE (and the pointers
210:  * by which a thread is bucketed under its group). The channel is RLS-aware
211:  * via the user filter, so the client only receives rows it is allowed to see.
212:  *
213:  * Returns a `refetch` function so dialogs/actions that mutate data (create
214:  * group, create thread, delete, rename) can immediately refresh the sidebar
215:  * without waiting for the realtime event — useful when realtime isn't
216:  * enabled on the project or the change originates from a different client.
217:  */
218: export function useSidebarData(workspaceId: string): SidebarData & {
219: 	refetch: () => void;
220: } {
221: 	const [data, setData] = useState<SidebarData>({
222: 		user: null,
223: 		workspaces: [],
224: 		groups: [],
225: 		loading: true,
226: 	});
227: 
228: 	const dataRef = useRef(data);
229: 	dataRef.current = data;
230: 
231: 	const supabaseRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof getBrowserSupabase> | null>(
232: 		null,
233: 	);
234: 	const userIdRef = useRef<string>("");
235: 	const refreshFromDbRef = useRef<(() => void) | null>(null);
236: 	const channelRef = useRef<
237: 		Awaited<ReturnType<ReturnType<typeof getBrowserSupabase>["channel"]>> | null
238: 	>(null);
239: 
240: 	useEffect(() => {
241: 		let cancelled = false;
242: 
243: 		async function load() {
244: 			setData((d) => ({ ...d, loading: true }));
245: 			const supabase = getBrowserSupabase();
246: 			supabaseRef.current = supabase;
247: 
248: 			const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
249: 			if (!user) {
250: 				if (!cancelled) {
251: 					setData({ user: null, workspaces: [], groups: [], loading: false });
252: 				}
253: 				return;
254: 			}
255: 			userIdRef.current = user.id;
256: 
257: 			const sidebarData = await fetchSidebarData(
258: 				supabase,
259: 				user.id,
260: 				workspaceId,
261: 				null,
262: 			);
263: 			if (cancelled) return;
264: 			setData(sidebarData);
265: 
266: 			// Realtime channel: keep groups + threads in sync for this
267: 			// workspace. RLS-scoped via the user config, so the client only
268: 			// receives rows it is allowed to see.
269: 			const channel = supabase.channel(`workspace:${workspaceId}`, {
270: 				config: { user: { id: user.id } },
271: 			}).on(
272: 				"postgres_changes",
273: 				{
274: 					event: "*",
275: 					table: "groups",
276: 					filter: `workspace_id = '${workspaceId}'`,
277: 				},
278: 				() => {
279: 					if (cancelled) return;
280: 					refreshFromDbRef.current?.();
281: 				},
282: 			).on(
283: 				"postgres_changes",
284: 				{
285: 					event: "*",
286: 					table: "threads",
287: 					filter: `workspace_id = '${workspaceId}'`,
288: 				},
289: 				() => {
290: 					if (cancelled) return;
291: 					refreshFromDbRef.current?.();
292: 				},
293: 			).subscribe();
294: 			channelRef.current = channel;
295: 
296: 			// Store the refresh closure so the public refetch + realtime
297: 			// callbacks both call the same function.
298: 			refreshFromDbRef.current = () =>
299: 				fetchSidebarData(supabase, user.id, workspaceId, dataRef.current).then(
300: 					(setData),
301: 				);
302: 		}
303: 
304: 		load();
305: 		return () => {
306: 			cancelled = true;
307: 			channelRef.current?.unsubscribe();
308: 		};
309: 	}, [workspaceId]);
310: 
311: 	const refetch = () => {
312: 		if (!supabaseRef.current || !userIdRef.current) return;
313: 		refreshFromDbRef.current?.();
314: 	};
315: 
316: 	return { ...data, refetch };
317: }
